events.title: Liverpool and Manchester Railway opens
events.description: The world's first intercity passenger railway, running entirely on steam power, opened between Liverpool and Manchester. During the celebrations, MP William Huskisson was struck by Stephenson's locomotive Rocket and died, which made him one of the first widely reported railway fatalities.
events.significance: The line showed that steam railways could carry passengers and freight on a regular schedule. That set the template for railways around the world, and the accident was an early warning about their dangers.

events.title: Central America declares independence from Spain
events.description: The Province of Guatemala proclaimed independence from the Spanish Empire. The declaration covered much of Central America, including present-day Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica.
events.significance: The date is still celebrated as Independence Day in several Central American countries. It marked the end of three centuries of Spanish colonial rule in the region.

events.title: Tanks debut at the Battle of the Somme
events.description: British forces used tanks in battle for the first time during the Somme offensive in northern France. The new armored vehicles were meant to break the deadlock of trench warfare.
events.significance: The first tanks were slow and unreliable. Even so, they began a new era of mechanized warfare that reshaped armies for the rest of the century.

events.title: Nuremberg Laws enacted in Nazi Germany
events.description: The Nazi regime announced laws that stripped German Jews of their citizenship and banned marriage between Jews and non-Jews. The same day, Germany adopted the swastika flag as its national flag.
events.significance: The laws gave legal form to racial persecution in Germany. They were a major step on the path toward the Holocaust.

events.title: US forces land at Inchon
events.description: During the Korean War, United States-led forces made an amphibious landing at Inchon on the west coast of Korea.
events.significance: The landing turned the course of the early war. It let UN forces retake the initiative and recapture Seoul.
